definitions.explanation: A flat piece of unused land covered in grass and weeds, especially one in or near a town where children play. Informal and everyday in tone.

examples.english: To play in the open field.

examples.japanese: {家|いえ}の{裏|うら}に{広|ひろ}い{原|はら}っぱがある。
examples.english: There is a wide grassy lot behind the house.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}は、{近所|きんじょ}の{原|はら}っぱで{日|ひ}が{暮|く}れるまで{野球|やきゅう}をしていた。
examples.english: When I was a child, I played baseball in the neighborhood field until the sun went down.

notes:
{原|はら} (field, plain) plus the informal suffix っぱ. The word carries a nostalgic, childhood flavor and appears often in stories about growing up.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {原|はら}っぱで{遊|あそ}ぶ: to play in the field
- {草|くさ}っ{原|ぱら}: a grassy patch (a related informal word with the parts reversed)
- {広|ひろ}い{原|はら}っぱ: a wide open field

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {野原|のはら}: field, meadow — more neutral and literary, often out in the countryside
- {空|あ}き{地|ち}: vacant lot — emphasizes that the land is unused or awaiting development, with no suggestion of grass
